final.title: Measure email threading before you automate it
final.body:
If you are thinking about email threading, treat it as a workflow decision first, not a software feature. The real question is whether you are losing time because replies are hard to follow, context is split across inboxes, or follow-ups keep drifting. If that happens only now and then, automation is probably the wrong place to spend attention. A cleaner mailbox habit may be enough.

The practical next step is manual: review one week of email activity and mark every thread that went off track. Note why it happened, how long it took to recover, and whether the same problem repeats. That gives you a real measure of the cost before anyone tries to fix it with tools. No need to turn every inbox wobble into a project; email already has enough drama.

If the same threading issue keeps showing up, the bounded decision is whether to tune your existing email or CRM setup, or whether the problem is specific enough to justify a small AI-assisted pilot for categorisation or routing. Keep that pilot narrow. Do not mix it with bulk email, compliance-heavy correspondence, or anything that would require autonomous decisions. Human approval stays in place for any high-risk step.
